sources.entry: cmd+x - Launch Activity Monitor with Ctrl+Opt+Delete, cut and move files in Finder with Cmd+X.

summary.name: cmd+x
summary.one_liner: A free Mac utility that adds Windows-style cut-and-move to Finder with Command+X and opens Activity Monitor with Control+Option+Delete.
use_cases: Moving files in Finder with cut and paste instead of copy and delete
Opening Activity Monitor quickly from the keyboard
Adopting Windows keyboard habits on a Mac
Running a background keyboard shortcut helper at login
summary.what_it_does: cmd+x is a Mac app that adds a true cut-then-move workflow in Finder: Command+X cuts files and Command+V moves them. It also opens Activity Monitor with Control+Option+Delete, and that shortcut can be customized. The app can start at login and hide its Dock icon. A floating HUD shows Command+X instructions with optional system sound cues. The page states that the app does not collect personal data and performs all operations locally on the Mac.
notable: Command+X and Command+V give Finder a cut-then-move workflow
Control+Option+Delete opens Activity Monitor, with a customizable shortcut
Can start at login and hide the Dock icon
Does not collect data; operations run locally
caveats: Offers in-app purchases (a $1.99 'Buy me a coffee' tip is listed)
